description: Varispeed: changes the speed and pitch of the sound together, like re-clocking a tape. Pinned to submode 2 (transposition in fractional semitones — the more musical control surface). Submode 1 is the same process parameterized as a speed ratio; submodes 3/4 only print information; 5 is accel/decel and 6 is vibrato — all can be curated separately later. Duration model verified against the r8 binary to within 0.01% across ±12, +7 and -5 semitones on 1–3 s inputs.
musical_use: The tape-speed transposition: pitch and duration move together, preserving the source's internal coherence (unlike independent pitch-shift or time-stretch). -12 doubles the duration an octave down; +12 halves it an octave up. Fractional values give detunings for thickening layers. With a breakpoint file for semitones, you get glissandi and tape-wobble effects — the transposition contour is followed smoothly across the file.

semitones.description: Transposition in (possibly fractional) semitones, relative to the original speed. Positive = higher and faster (shorter output); negative = lower and slower (longer output); 0 = no change. CDP accepts at least ±96 (verified; -96 multiplies duration by 256 — mind the output length). Musically useful range is roughly ±24. May vary over time via a breakpoint file; by default breakpoint times are read as infile times (see known_issues for the -o switch).

examples.description: Drop the source an octave: half speed, double duration.
examples.expected_use: Classic octave-down slowdown — darker, heavier version of the source with all internal relationships intact.

examples.description: Detune up a quarter-tone for layering against the original.
examples.expected_use: Thicken a texture by mixing slightly-transposed copies.

known_issues: The -o switch (read breakpoint times as outfile times instead of infile times) is a value-less flag not exposed in the curated parameters (same policy as extend loop's -b). Reach for execute() if you need it.

With a breakpoint-valued semitones the duration model cannot predict output length (the engine skips pre-flight prediction for breakpoint params); the output ends when the infile is exhausted at the varying speed.
